abilityauxiliary.name: Experience Sets In
abilityauxiliary.precondition: Luck Fate result or Critical Success or Failure on a physical attack on a creature of the given specialization.
abilityauxiliary.effect: +Rank to all further physical attacks by this character against that creature.

abilitydescription.p: The character bears an animosity towards, and/or has been trained to fight opponents of a given monster-class.

This ability is triggered after a character with this ability makes their first successful blessed melee attack against a creature having a monster-class that this character is adversarial to. Once triggered the characters training/experience kicks in and the ability remains active for the rest of the combat.
While triggered the character gains a bonus equal to their adversary rank for combat checks against monsters of the given monster-class (the bonus is to the check only and not to damage).

The character takes the brunt of the attack on their armour, hoping that it will protect them. The bonus for this check is determined by the armour the character is wearing. A character may be harder to hit because they are wearing armour or carrying a shield.

ability:armour Armour Check After the character gets attacked they make an armour check to see if that attack was successfully defeated by the characters armour. If successful the character takes no damage from the attack. This can be interpreted as either the armour taking the force of the blow and protecting the character, or the character moving in such a way that the the character is struck a glancing blow leaving them uninjured.

Instead of making an armour check the character may choose to dodge, shield block, parry or use some other attack-reaction ability. Armour is not a reaction and does not use the characters reaction for the current turn unlike many other defence check abilities.

To make an Armour Check the modifier is calculated as follows. First calculate the bonus for the type of armour worn by the character, Plate provides +1, No armour provides -3. If the character is wielding a shield they get a shield bonus of +1. The Armour Ability Modifier is then the Armour Bonus plus the Shield bonus plus Rank of their Armour ability.

If the armour result fails and a boon is rolled the attack deals half damage. If the armour result fails and a bane is rolled the attack deals double damage. If the armour check succeeds the attack does no damage. If it fails the attack does normal damage.
Some attacks cannot be defended with armour, a dragons breath weapon. If no other attack-reaction ability is used the attack automatically does normal damage.

After your character makes a successful melee attack you can make a Blood Frenzy Check. If successful you enter a Blood Frenzy and get advantage for standard basic melee attacks. While in a frenzy the character must perform a basic melee attack every turn, moving to attack if necessary. The frenzy ends when the character runs out of Mettle, or when they perform a turn without attacking anything, or when they make a free Mettle Check to control themselves. While in a frenzy if the character cannot reach an enemy then they must attack an ally.
The character must pay the pool cost each round to maintain this ability.

Brawling is the art of unarmed combat. It involves grappling, head butting, punching, or knocking out opponents. The check has a -3 penalty against larger creatures, and a -6 penalty against much larger creatures.

Grappling See Brawl/Grappling
Grappling involves grabbing, tackling or wrestling an opponent and holding them without harming them. Other attacks against a grappled opponent are hindered by the grappler being close to the opponent and the opponents struggling. Every round that an opponent is grappled they may make an opposed Brawl|Str test against their grappler to escape. Once grappled it takes a round for a second character to tie-up, or otherwise constrain, the opponent.

Head Butt See Brawl/Head Butt
A Head Butt involves the attacker driving their head into the bridge of the defenders nose. Head butting is mainly used as an attack of last resort or as a surprise attack. An attacker may only head butt someone immediately in front or behind them. An character may head butt when grappled or otherwise constrained. Head butts do 1d3+Str damage, +1 damage if the attacker is wearing a helmet and -1 damage if the defender is wearing a helmet.

Punch See Brawl/Punch
Kick See Brawl/Kick
When a character makes a Punch or Kick attack the attacker attempts to hit their opponent using their fists. The attack is a Brawl vs Targets Defence. It does 1d3+Str damage, +2 damage if the attacker is wearing gauntlets, -2 damage if the attacker is wearing a helmet.

Knockout See Brawl/Knockout
Subdue See Brawl/Knockout
After a character reduces an opponents hit points to zero using a Brawl attack or when attacking with a non-lethal weapon, they may make an attempt to knock the opponent out instead of killing them Brawl vs DC 13. If the character succeeds in their check the opponent becomes Unconscious. If the check fails then the opponent is killed.

abilityauxiliary.name: Talent
abilityauxiliary.precondition: Bane with a Success in a melee attack against an opponent of Appropriate Size
abilityauxiliary.effect: Make a Brawl attack with a Dirty Fighter Rank bonus.

abilitydescription.p: When the character makes a successful melee attack with a bane, they may immediately make a Brawl attack as a minor action adding their Dirty-Fighter Rank to any damage that the Brawl attack does.

ability:dodge The character may attempt to dodge, to leap out of the way of the attack, instead of making an armour roll. Doing so uses the characters reaction for the round. If successful the attack is dodged and the character takes no damage.

Some types of attack cannot be dodged, e.g. surprise attacks or poisonous gas attacks. Other types of attack the acid or fire attacks of dragons may be dodgeable depending on the context and deal half or no damage (at the GM's discretion).

Once per movement the attacker may use his mass and strength to brush aside those whostand in his way. Such is the force of his unstoppable charge that at most one opportunity attack can be made against him. The pushed opponent cannot make an opportunity attack against the Juggernaut.
Note that the Juggernaut ability may only be used against opponents of similar or smaller size and strength.

ability:parry When a character is attacked they may attempt to parry the blow when using a mace or sword instead of making an armour roll. If the parry result fails and a boon is rolled the attack deals half damage. If the parry result fails and a bane is rolled the attack deals double damage. It may not be possible to parry certain types of attack, for example breath weapons cannot be parried.
When the characters hit points drop to 0 they can instantly make a Retribution check and if successful the character may immediately perform a Charge or an Attack.
In the event of an overcharge the character gains the Unconscious condition at the end of their action.
